requirements.quote: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the limits for rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection are those defined in IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5: - The value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0; - The value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65; - The value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms; - The relative steady-state voltage change, dc, shall not exceed 3.3 per cent; - The maximum relative voltage change dmax, shall not exceed 6 per cent.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, the limits for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection are those defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5: - The value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0; - The value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65; - The value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms; - The relative steady-state voltage change, dc, shall not exceed 3.3 per cent; - The maximum relative voltage change dmax, shall not exceed 6 per cent.
requirements.quote: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, the limits for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection are those defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5: - The value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0; - The value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65; - The value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms; - The relative steady-state voltage change, dc, shall not exceed 3.3 per cent; - The maximum relative voltage change dmax, shall not exceed 6 per cent.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, the value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0.
requirements.quote: The value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0;

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, the value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65.
requirements.quote: The value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65;

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, the value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms.
requirements.quote: The value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms;

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, the relative steady-state voltage change, dc, shall not exceed 3.3 per cent.
requirements.quote: The relative steady-state voltage change, dc, shall not exceed 3.3 per cent;

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, the maximum relative voltage change dmax shall not exceed 6 per cent.
requirements.quote: The maximum relative voltage change dmax, shall not exceed 6 per cent.

requirements.text: The application for approval shall be accompanied by a list of the devices prescribed by the manufacturer for the lighting and light-signalling assembly, in triplicate.
requirements.quote: A list of the devices prescribed by the manufacturer for the lighting and light-signalling assembly.

requirements.text: Each type of device in the list accompanying the application for approval shall be duly identified (component, type-approval mark, name of manufacturer, etc.).
requirements.quote: Each type shall be duly identified (component, type-approval mark, name of manufacturer, etc.), in addition the list may include in respect of each function the additional annotation "or equivalent devices";

requirements.text: The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, except that, if the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the frequency range in 14 frequency bands and perform tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band.
requirements.quote: The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the vehicle and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from any ESA.
requirements.quote: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the vehicle and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from any ESA.

requirements.text: The field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
requirements.quote: The background to the sample and the framework of the sample holder should be matt black and the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.

requirements.text: The residual stray light value, measured when the sample is covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap, shall be subtracted from that measured on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.quote: This value shall be subtracted from that measured on the retro-reflective device

requirements.text: The rear lamp shall be considered to satisfy the conformity requirements from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.quote: The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

requirements.text: In the case of non-replaceable filament light source(s) or light source module(s) equipped with non-replaceable filament light source, at any conformity of production check, the holder of the type approval shall demonstrate the use in normal production and show the identification of the non-replaceable filament light source(s) as indicated in the type approval documentation.
requirements.quote: the holder of the type approval shall demonstrate the use in normal production and show the identification of the non-replaceable filament light source(s) as indicated in the type approval documentation;

requirements.text: Reflections from the floor and walls which occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.
requirements.quote: Reflections from the floor and walls which occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

requirements.text: If the type of lamp(s) submitted for approval in pursuance of paragraph 3.1. meets the requirements of this Regulation, approval shall be granted.
requirements.quote: If the type of lamp(s) submitted for approval in pursuance of paragraph 3.1. meets the requirements of this Regulation, approval shall be granted.

requirements.text: All the devices of an interdependent lamp system must be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.
requirements.quote: All the devices of an interdependent lamp system must be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.

requirements.text: For each type of lamp, the holder of the type approval shall carry out at least the following tests, at appropriate intervals.
requirements.quote: For each type of lamp, the holder of the type approval shall carry out at least the following tests, at appropriate intervals.

requirements.text: The tests shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.
requirements.quote: The tests shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.

requirements.text: If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested.
requirements.quote: If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested.

requirements.text: The manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
requirements.quote: The manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.

requirements.text: The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles.
requirements.quote: The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles; however the SM2 type of side-marker lamps may be used on the M1 category of vehicles.

requirements.text: On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used, if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
requirements.quote: In addition, on M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used, if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.

requirements.text: Side-marker lamps shall be present on all vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m, except for chassis-cabs.
requirements.quote: Presence Mandatory: On all vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m, except for chassis-cabs.

requirements.text: The limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
requirements.quote: The limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

requirements.text: For testing the daytime colour and luminance factor of the material, measurements shall be done with a spectrophotometer in accordance with the provisions of Publication CIE 15:2004, Recommendations on Colorimetry - Second Edition, either illuminated poly-chromatically or with a monochromator providing stepwise the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 at an angle 45º to the normal and viewed along the normal (geometry 45/0).
requirements.quote: Measurements shall be done with a spectrophotometer in accordance with the provisions of Publication CIE 15:2004, Recommendations on Colorimetry - Second Edition, either illuminated poly-chromatically or with a monochromator providing stepwise the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) at an angle 45º to the normal and viewed along the normal (geometry 45/0).

requirements.text: When a monochromator providing stepwise the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 is used, the stepwise resolution Δλ shall be not larger than 10 nm.
requirements.quote: In the latter case, the stepwise resolution Δλ shall be not larger than 10 nm.

requirements.text: Where similar simulation spectra are used, the quality of the D65 simulation shall be assessed by the method described in ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004.
requirements.quote: Alternatively, similar simulation spectra are allowed, if verified that the colorimetric measuring procedure is of the same accuracy, meaning that the quality of the D65 simulation shall be assessed by the method described in ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004.

requirements.text: The spectral distribution of the Illuminant shall be in category BC (CIELAB) or better.
requirements.quote: The spectral distribution of the Illuminant shall be in category BC (CIELAB) or better.

requirements.text: The measurement area shall be at least minimum 4.0 cm².
requirements.quote: The measurement area shall be at least minimum 4.0 cm².

requirements.text: The apertures of the light source and the receiver shall have sufficient dimensions in proportion to distances to ensure compliance with the above-mentioned recommendations.
requirements.quote: In addition, the apertures of the light source and the receiver shall have sufficient dimensions in proportion to distances to ensure compliance with the above-mentioned recommendations.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test level for AC or DC power lines shall be ± 2 kV test voltage in open circuit.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ± 2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test rise time (Tr) for AC or DC power lines shall be 5 ns.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ± 2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test hold time (Th) for AC or DC power lines shall be 50 ns.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ± 2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test repetition rate for AC or DC power lines shall be 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ± 2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test level for AC or DC power lines shall be ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test rise time (Tr) for AC or DC power lines shall be 5 ns.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test hold time (Th) for AC or DC power lines shall be 50 ns.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test repetition rate for AC or DC power lines shall be 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.
requirements.quote: If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test levels, for AC or DC power lines, shall be: ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, and a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz for at least 1 minute.

requirements.text: The requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. shall be applicable to stop- and position lamps for vehicles of category L.
requirements.quote: However, the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. and paragraph 4.6.1.2. (a) are still applicable.

requirements.text: The requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2. (a) shall be applicable to stop- and position lamps for vehicles of category L.
requirements.quote: However, the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. and paragraph 4.6.1.2. (a) are still applicable.

requirements.text: The conformity of production procedures for the rear lamp shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the following requirements:
requirements.quote: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the following requirements:

requirements.text: The requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. shall be applicable to rear registration plate lamps, except that the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2. do not apply to rear registration plate lamps.
requirements.quote: The requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2. do not apply to rear registration plate lamps. However, the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. are still applicable.

requirements.text: The conformity of production procedures for the rear lamp shall comply with those set out in the Agreement, Appendix 2 (E/ECE/324-E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.2), with the following requirements:
requirements.quote: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the Agreement, Appendix 2 (E/ECE/324-E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.2), with the following requirements:

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 5.2.4.5., every retro-reflective marking shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.quote: Every retro-reflective marking, when tested according to paragraph 5.2.4.5., shall meet: (a) The dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5;

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 5.2.4.5., every retro-reflective marking shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.2.5. and 5.2.6.
requirements.quote: (b) The photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.2.5. and 5.2.6.; and

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 5.2.4.5., every retro-reflective marking shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.2.7.
requirements.quote: (c) The physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.2.7.

requirements.text: For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.9.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the front position lamp horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.quote: Horizontal angle: 45° outwards to 45° inwards. However, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

requirements.text: For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.9.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the front position lamp vertical angle of geometric visibility shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.quote: Vertical angle: 15° above and below the horizontal. However, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

requirements.text: To be considered visible, the front position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm2.
requirements.quote: To be considered visible, the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm2.

requirements.text: The illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
requirements.quote: The illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

requirements.text: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the retro-reflective marking material samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 3 of Annex 6, prior to the tests described in Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 6.
requirements.quote: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 3 of Annex 6, prior to the tests described in Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 6.

requirements.text: The front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 30° inwards and outwards, except that in the case of trailers, the angle inwards may be reduced to 10°.
requirements.quote: Horizontal angle: 30° inwards and outwards. In the case of trailers, the angle inwards may be reduced to 10°.

requirements.text: If because of the construction of the trailers the horizontal visibility angle cannot be met by the mandatory retro-reflectors, additional (supplementary) retro-reflectors shall be fitted, without the width limitation (paragraph 6.16.4.1.), which shall, in conjunction with the mandatory retro-reflectors, give the necessary visibility angle.
requirements.quote: If because of the construction of the trailers this angle cannot be met by the mandatory retro-reflectors, then additional (supplementary) retro-reflectors shall be fitted, without the width limitation (paragraph 6.16.4.1. above), which shall, in conjunction with the mandatory retro-reflectors, give the necessary visibility angle.

requirements.text: The front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 10° above and below the horizontal, except that where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.quote: Vertical angle: 10° above and below the horizontal. However, where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.

requirements.text: In the case of adhesive materials, a specimen of the retro-reflective marking sample unit shall be subjected to a bonding strength test as specified in Part 2 of Annex 8.
requirements.quote: Bonding strength (in the case of adhesive materials) A specimen of the sample unit shall be subjected to a test as specified in Part 2 of Annex 8.

requirements.text: The point on the illuminating surface of the rear triangular retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.quote: In width: that point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

requirements.text: The inner edges of the rear triangular retro-reflectors shall not be less than 600 mm apart, except that this distance may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
requirements.quote: The inner edges of the retro-reflectors shall not be less than 600 mm apart. This distance may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

requirements.text: The testing of the day-time colour for the retro-reflective device shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.2.
requirements.quote: The testing of the day-time colour for retro-reflective device shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.2.

requirements.text: In case the luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp is intended to be reduced, according to the relevant requirements of paragraph 6.19.7. of the 08 or any of the subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 48, the reduced designed maximum luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp shall not exceed 1.40∙102 cd.
requirements.quote: In case the luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp is intended to be reduced, according to the relevant requirements of paragraph 6.19.7. of the 08 or any of the subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 48, the reduced designed maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 1.40∙102 cd.

requirements.text: If, in the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source and if results of the test described above do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
requirements.quote: If, in the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source and if results of the test described above do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.

requirements.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide evidence (if requested by the test authority) that vehicle performance is not adversely affected by such transmitters.
requirements.quote: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide evidence (if requested by the test authority) that vehicle performance is not adversely affected by such transmitters.

requirements.text: The tests of conformity of the retro-reflective device in this Regulation shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
requirements.quote: Tests of conformity in this Regulation shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performance, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
requirements.quote: (a) No measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performance, if, in the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source and if results of the test described above do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
requirements.quote: (b) If, in the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source and if results of the test described above do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.

requirements.text: The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent.
requirements.quote: The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent.

requirements.text: If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 shall be applied.
requirements.quote: In this case the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 shall be applied.

requirements.text: The manufacturer of the rear registration plate illuminating lamp shall specify one or more or a field of positions in which the device is to be fitted in relation to the space for the registration plate; when the lamp is placed in the position(s) specified by the manufacturer the angle of incidence of the light on the surface of the plate does not exceed 82° at any point on the surface to be illuminated, this angle being measured from the extremity of the device's illuminating area which is furthest from the surface of the plate.

The ESA radiated broadband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver, using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2.

Where method TM1 (black-standard thermometer) is used, the retro-reflector samples shall be exposed using cycle No. 1 according to EN ISO 4892-2:2013 with an exposure period of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband (340 nm) irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², a black-standard temperature of 65 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 50 ± 10 %.

Where method TM2 (black-panel thermometer) is used, the retro-reflector samples shall be exposed using cycle No. 4 according to EN ISO 4892-2:2013 with an exposure period of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband (340 nm) irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², a black-panel temperature of 63 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 50 ± 10 %.
The rear lamp's retro-reflective device samples shall be prepared in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
After about 5 minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
After cleaning, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

After the outer surface of the retro-reflective device has been wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil, after about 5 minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
The RI shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
The concealment of the rear position lamp, the stop lamp and the reversing lamp shall be prohibited.
The direction-indicator lamp shall emit amber light.
The main-beam headlamp shall be white.
The dipped-beam headlamp shall be white.
The front fog lamp shall be white or selective yellow.
The hazard warning signal shall be amber.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall be amber.
The parking lamp shall be white in front, red at the rear, amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.

The side-marker lamp shall be amber, except that the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The front retro-reflector, non-triangular shall be identical to incident light8.

The side retro-reflector, non-triangular shall be amber, except that the rearmost side retro-reflector can be red if it is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear position lamp, the rear end outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop-lamp, the red rearmost side-marker lamp or the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular.
The conspicuity marking shall be white to the front, white or yellow to the side, and red or yellow to the rear.
The adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS) shall be white.
The exterior courtesy lamp shall be white.
The exterior courtesy lamp shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the exterior courtesy lamp.
The manoeuvring lamp shall be white.
The answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The reversing projection shall be white.
The rear conspicuity marking shall emit red or yellow light.
The rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, shall be installed on movable components only.

In the case of dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps, the requirement to return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer shall be considered satisfied if, when the movable components are moved and returned to the normal position 10 times, no value of the angular inclination of these lamps, relative to its support, measured after each operation of the movable component, differs by more than 0.15 per cent from the average of the 10 measured values.

If the value of 0.15 per cent is exceeded, each limit specified in paragraph 6.2.6.1.1. shall then be modified by this excess to decrease the allowed range of inclinations when checking the vehicle according to Annex 6.

If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable and additional lamps are not provided, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark shall be deemed not to be present when the lamp cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Where the rear lamp is approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.
In the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

Where variable luminous intensity control responds to traffic conditions independent from environmental conditions mentioned under 5.26.1., a decrease of the luminous intensity, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, may be applied only as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m, except that as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h the intensity decrease already activated may remain active.

For vehicles of M and N categories, the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service responsible for type approval testing that the electric power supply conditions for the devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. above comply, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, with the following provisions.

The devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. above shall not be supplied with a voltage exceeding the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.
No account is taken of obstacles, if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
For the orientation of the reference axis of the light-signalling devices, in each direction a tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed.
In each direction a tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed.
The reference axis of all other signalling devices shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
In the case where an AFS is installed, the rear lamp shall be verified with the system in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
The requirements for single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a) shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

The maximum height above the ground of the lamp shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, except that where the (maximum and minimum) height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light.
In the absence of specific instructions, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
The rear position lamps shall be two.
The rear position lamp shall be not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
The rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal.
For M1 and N1 category vehicles, where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards.
When determining the unobstructed apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular may be optional on trailers provided that it is grouped together with the other rear light-signalling devices.
Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular shall be optional on trailers.
The number of rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be two.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular shall be not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 900 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 1,200 mm above the ground if grouped with any rear lamp(s).
The emergency stop signal shall be present on motor vehicles.
The reversing lamp shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
One reversing lamp device shall be mandatory on motor vehicles of category M1.
A second reversing lamp device may be installed as optional on motor vehicles of category M1.
The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
When Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the angle α shall be 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
If the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. are fitted on the side of the vehicle, the vertical aim of the two optional devices may be directed downwards.
Devices of S3 or S4 category of the stop lamp may be installed on other categories of vehicles as optional.

For S3 or S4 category stop lamps on all other categories of vehicles, the centre of reference shall be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, except that where two S3 or S4 category stop lamps are installed according to paragraph 6.7.2.
If the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible.
For S1 or S2 categories devices, the stop lamp shall be not less than 350 mm above the ground.

The stop lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices the horizontal angle shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
The stop lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices the vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.
The stop lamps shall not be required to function if the device, which starts and/or stops the propulsion system, is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
